experiment.title: DDX3X SGE Exon 1
experiment.abstractText: This dataset contains the cLFC and cLFC-trend for DDX3X saturation genome editing (SGE) data from Exon 1. Variants were assayed based on viability in LIG4-KO HAP1 cells after direct editing of the endogenous DDX3X locus using CRISPR-based editing.
experiment.methodText: Oligo pools containing the designed variants (eg. exonic and intronic SNV, inframe codon deletion) were synthesized and cloned into the HDR plasmids with ~800bp of each targeted exon homology arm. The designed oligos contain the variants being assayed and 1-3 fixed synonymous substitutions at the PAM and protospacer to prevent re-editing by Cas9 after a successful repair. LIG4-KO HAP1 cells with Cas9 overexpression were co-transfected with a plasmid expressing sgRNA and the puromycin-resistant gene together with the HDR plasmid library. The transfected cells were selected with puromycin for 48 hours and sampled on Day4, Day 7, Day11, Day15 and Day21. cLFC was calculated for Day 7, Day 11, Day15 and Day21 with Day4 as a baseline. cLFC-trend was calculated for Day15 with Day4 as a baseline. Samples were sequenced with 300 bases single-end read using Illumina Hiseq 2500 Rapid.

scoreSets.shortDescription: DDX3X SGE scores for clinical use

experiment.title: DDX3X SGE scores for clinical use
experiment.shortDescription: DDX3X SGE scores for clinical use
experiment.abstractText: This dataset contains a score intended for clinical use in the context of a patient being assessed for DDX3X-related neurodevelopmental disorder. This is a score of nucleotide-variant functional effect derived from saturation genome editing performed in LIG4-KO HAP1 cells for the gene DDX3X. Saturation genome editing identifies variants that result in loss of DDX3X function. Variants are created by directly editing the endogenous DNA locus. Therefore, this technique will identify variants that alter splicing.
experiment.methodText:
We performed Saturation genome editing on DDX3X and quantified variant abundance at 5 time points. A Random Forest supervised classifier was constructed, using combined log fold-change of variant abundance (cLFC, a combined measure of variant abundance from two independent sgRNA experiments) at day 7, 11 and 15 compared to day 4, post-transfection. For raw cLFC values, see exon-specific MAVEdb entries listed above.
Variant training dataset: Variants observed in the GnomAD and UKBB population databases and benign/likely benign variants deposited in ClinVar and DECIPHER were used as ‘negative truth set’ variants (n=540). ‘Positive truth set’ variants (n=168) were de novo likely pathogenic and pathogenic variants curated from ClinVar; DECIPHER; Genomics England 100,000 genomes study; Kaplanis and Samocha et al. 2020 and Lennox et al., 2020. Please see Radford and Tan et al. 2023 for more details. Stratified sampling was used to select 80% of these truth set variants to train the model. 
Model performance: Random Forest model performance estimated from ‘test truth variants’ not used to train the model, using a posterior probability threshold of 50%, was 97.1% sensitivity and 100% specificity. However, we accept that in some clinical decision-making contexts a posterior-probability of variant function higher than 50% may be desirable. Therefore, we propose that for clinical use a posterior probability of > 90% be considered high confidence, and posterior probability 50-90% be considered intermediate confidence.

The score given in the table below is the posterior-probability from this Random Forest model that a variant is non-functional in the context of DDX3X-related neurodevelopmental disorder. In the column “SGE_prediction_of_variant_function_in_NDD_context” variants are classed as ‘abnormal’ if their Random Forest posterior probability is > 0.5. Variants are classed as “High_confidence” in the column “Confidence_of_functionally_abnormal_variant_prediction” if their Random Forest posterior probability is > 0.9. Variants are classed as “Intermediate_confidence” if their Random Forest posterior probability is between 0.5 and 0.9.

primaryPublicationIdentifiers.title: Saturation genome editing of DDX3X clarifies pathogenicity of germline and somatic variation.
primaryPublicationIdentifiers.abstract: Loss-of-function of DDX3X is a leading cause of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD) in females. DDX3X is also a somatically mutated cancer driver gene proposed to have tumour promoting and suppressing effects. We perform saturation genome editing of DDX3X, testing in vitro the functional impact of 12,776 nucleotide variants. We identify 3432 functionally abnormal variants, in three distinct classes. We train a machine learning classifier to identify functionally abnormal variants of NDD-relevance. This classifier has at least 97% sensitivity and 99% specificity to detect variants pathogenic for NDD, substantially out-performing in silico predictors, and resolving up to 93% of variants of uncertain significance. Moreover, functionally-abnormal variants can account for almost all of the excess nonsynonymous DDX3X somatic mutations seen in DDX3X-driven cancers. Systematic maps of variant effects generated in experimentally tractable cell types have the potential to transform clinical interpretation of both germline and somatic disease-associated variation.
primaryPublicationIdentifiers.referenceHtml: Radford EJ, et al. Saturation genome editing of DDX3X clarifies pathogenicity of germline and somatic variation. Nat Commun. 2023; 14:7702. 10.1038/s41467-023-43041-4

experiment.title: Saturation genome essentiality screen of DDX3X in HAP1 cells
experiment.shortDescription: Saturation genome essentiality screen of DDX3X in HAP1 cells (log fold change at day 15)
experiment.abstractText: Loss-of-function of _DDX3X_ is a leading cause of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD) in females. _DDX3X_ is also a somatically mutated cancer driver gene proposed to have tumour promoting and suppressing effects. We perform saturation genome editing of _DDX3X_, testing in vitro the functional impact of 12,776 nucleotide variants. We identify 3432 functionally abnormal variants, in three distinct classes. We train a machine learning classifier to identify functionally abnormal variants of NDD-relevance. This classifier has at least 97% sensitivity and 99% specificity to detect variants pathogenic for NDD, substantially out-performing in silico predictors, and resolving up to 93% of variants of uncertain significance. Moreover, functionally-abnormal variants can account for almost all of the excess nonsynonymous _DDX3X_ somatic mutations seen in _DDX3X_-driven cancers. Systematic maps of variant effects generated in experimentally tractable cell types have the potential to transform clinical interpretation of both germline and somatic disease-associated variation.
experiment.methodText: This study uses saturation genome editing (SGE) based essentiality screen to determine _DDX3X_ function.  HAP1 cells were transfected with sgRNA and HDR template library plasmids, followed by puromycin selection for two days. Cell pellets were harvested at several time points (Days 4, 7, 11, 15, and 21). Genomic DNA was extracted from these samples and direct sequencing was used to determine the variant frequency at each time point.

We train a machine learning classifier to identify functionally abnormal variants of NDD-relevance. This classifier has at least 97% sensitivity and 99% specificity to detect variants pathogenic for NDD, substantially out-performing in silico predictors, and resolving up to 93% of variants of uncertain significance. Moreover, functionally-abnormal variants can account for almost all of the excess nonsynonymous DDX3X somatic mutations seen in DDX3X-driven cancers. Systematic maps of variant effects generated in experimentally tractable cell types have the potential to transform clinical interpretation of both germline and somatic disease-associated variation.
